rows.en:
A sacrifice to a doll?
I couldn't believe a story like that.
There was no way such a thing could happen.
Something that horrifying...{p}

So it is a problem for you, then.
Well, of course it is.
After all, the theme of your paper is the seven wonders.
It only counts as the seven wonders when you have all seven scary stories, doesn't it?
...But still.
Let's just give it up gracefully, shall we?
You probably don't know this, but there's a story that if you hear seven scary stories about this school, something bad happens.
But since the seventh person still hasn't shown up, I can tell the sixth story without worrying.{p}

I think you can only find them innocently cute while you're a child.
I can't honestly think of dolls as cute.
Especially antique dolls.
I don't even want to think about the reasons a doll like that passed from hand to hand until it ended up here.
A soul dwells in a doll.
What if its emotions were swayed by the surroundings the doll is kept in?
Just thinking about it gives me chills.
Dolls don't come with a résumé.
You'd better not buy dolls carelessly.
Especially antique dolls...
Now, back to the story of the doll that lives in this school.{p}

Now that you mention it, maybe so.
They do say handmade dolls in particular feel warm.
The hands, feet and face of a doll, of course, and even its clothes or kimono are sewn by human hands, one stitch at a time.
So, precisely because they're handmade, the feelings packed into those dolls seem terribly strong, and I don't like that.
There's a famous doll maker in Japan, and they say the dolls that person makes laugh, get angry, move, and do all sorts of things.
Those dolls are indescribably mysterious: long, narrow eyes with large dark irises, and skin as white as can be, almost translucent.
And I sense something in that doll maker's dolls that draws people in.
I don't know what you meant, {a}{f:|}, when you said dolls are warm.
But once you hear this story, you won't be able to call dolls warm anymore.{p}

Yes, it's the story of the doll that lives in the school.
No one knows when that doll first came to this school.{p}

Does it make you feel nostalgic?
It seems you have memories of being fond of dolls when you were little, {a}{f:|}.
Children often won't let go of a favorite doll or stuffed animal until it falls to pieces.
Don't you often see children hugging dolls or stuffed animals that are stained with grime and covered in patches?
Even when their parents can't stand to watch anymore and say they'll buy a new one so the old one can be thrown out, the child absolutely won't listen.
Then one day, the child suddenly notices.
That they're no longer holding the doll or stuffed animal they once refused so fiercely to let go of...{p}

Little children often talk to all sorts of things, but maybe they really are having conversations with them.
We forget once we grow up, but when we were little, I'm sure we talked with all sorts of things like that too.
Do we lose the ability to talk with dolls when we grow up?
So what if the dolls, too, quietly vanish from around that child before anyone notices...
I'm sure some people would say, 'No, I threw it away.'
But is that really so?
Things have souls.
Dolls are shaped like people, aren't they?
That's why I think their feelings are even closer to a human's than those of other things.
Especially in childhood, we spend so much time with our dolls and stuffed animals.
I bet that's why a flood of nostalgia comes over you when you hear the word 'doll,' {a}{f:|}.{p}

Let's get back to the story of the doll in this school.
I suppose there are all kinds: dolls that have feelings of their own, dolls taken over by an evil spirit, and so on.
I can't say this too loudly, but...
I think the doll in this school is probably evil in itself, not something an evil spirit has possessed.
And so, no one knows when that doll first came to this school.{p}

When I was still little, there was a doll in my toy box that I couldn't possibly have owned.
It was a wind-up tin baby doll.
It laughed.
While its wind-up spring went whirr, whirr.
Even as a child, it gave me the creeps, and I asked my mother to take the doll away.
But when my mother looked in the toy box, that doll was nowhere to be found. Something like that happened once.
Maybe I was emotionally unstable back then.{p}

Anyway, what Kanai saw wasn't an illusion like the one I saw.
Anyone who was around him would have felt for certain that it was no illusion.{p}

Oh no, you can only say things like that for now.
Soon enough, you won't be laughing.
And then you'll be certain.
That the doll really does exist...{p}

You don't find it strange at all?
That's because you don't believe the doll exists, {a}{f:|}.
But the fact is, at least one person dies every single year without fail.
And what's more, every one of them ends up in a state like Kanai's.
I found it strange.
So I asked around among the people who knew the doll story.
And then I learned one fact.{p}

First of all, apparently the teachers are never harmed.
So they have nothing to do with it.
And the student, apparently, is chosen before they even enter the school.
It's only a rumor, mind you.
But they say the principal knows.
For some reason, among those who pass this school's entrance exam, there's always at least one person who actually failed.
And that person, apparently, is the sacrifice the doll has chosen.
So every year, a few students who should never have gotten into this school slip in.
The principal knows that.
The principal knows, and lets them in anyway.
The students who are meant to be sacrifices.
Apparently the doll sometimes takes a liking to someone other than the person meant to be the sacrifice.
When that happens, the sacrifice changes, or so they say...
On the other hand, if you become the sacrifice yourself, there's apparently just one way to escape.
Though they say the chances of it working are very slim.
Don't you think that's a terrifying story?{p}

"{f:I|I} need to hurry and tidy up in here and start putting the article together..."
It {f:seemed|looked like} someone had forgotten something and come back to the club room.
"Did you forget something?
That's fine.
{f:I'm|I'm} tied up right now, so {f:just go ahead and look|feel free to look} for it and take it with you."
{f:I|I} said it over my shoulder as I put the chairs away.{p}

When I turned around, {f:I|I} froze.
A child was standing in the doorway of the club room, staring right at me.
Pale skin, an expressionless face, big eyes and black hair: that was what struck {f:me|me}.
It seemed the child had been following {f:my|my} every move with {f:those|those} eyes for a while now.
A child, in a place like this?
No. This child {f:wasn't|wasn't} human.

You're pretty harsh, aren't you, {a}{f:|}?
You didn't have to say that.
Yes, I'm a pathetic person.
I'll admit that much.
But if you were in my shoes, {a}{f:|}, I think you'd have ended up doing what he said too.
I hurriedly packed my things into my bag while Kanai kept watch over me.{p}
The hallway was dead silent.

At that hour it was usually packed with students heading home, but for some reason there wasn't a soul around that day. It was dead silent.
I started walking side by side with Kanai.
Down the empty hallway...

"...I'm going to die today."
It came out of nowhere.
Who knows what got into him, but Kanai muttered that.
I didn't know what to say.
When I didn't answer, Kanai began talking on his own.
"...You know, for the past two or three days, I've been seeing the doll the whole time.
I know now, too.
Every year, this school has to offer up one sacrifice to the doll, right?"
And then he looked at me.{p}

My body was trembling.
I couldn't look Kanai in the face.
For some reason, I felt guilty.
I couldn't shake the feeling that Kanai was blaming me.
I couldn't shake the feeling that he resented me for knowing the doll story and not telling him.
I'm not responsible.
It's not my fault, either.
Besides, I only learned the doll story after it became clear he was the sacrifice.
Even so, my legs went rigid, and as I walked they felt as if they weren't my own.{p}

I felt like I was suffocating to death.
I kept my mouth shut, and it was all I could do to mechanically put one foot in front of the other.
"...The doll calls to me.
I don't know why the doll calls me.
Or why I was the one chosen...
But it's a fact that I'm being called.
And soon I'm going to die.
The doll won't leave me alone.
Look, it's right next to you even now.
Right now, you're walking between the doll and me."
With that, Kanai suddenly thrust his face right in front of mine as I tried to look away.{p}

His face was smiling.
Is that what a skull looks like when it smiles?
It was a terribly sad smile.
And I ended up meeting Kanai's gaze.
"...Look, the doll just put its hand on your shoulder.
What's wrong?
Can't you see it, Arai?
...Looks like the doll has taken a liking to you."
I wanted to run, but my legs wouldn't obey me.
As if I'd been hypnotized, my feet just kept moving forward.
My fear reached its peak.
If I had opened my mouth, my heart would have leapt right out of it.
Kanai laughed: hee hee hee...
When he laughed, his breath puffed across my face.
And how cold that breath was...{p}

"...The doll won't leave my side.
It even follows me home.
When I'm asleep, it stands by my pillow the whole time.
Just staring at me.
Is it real...?
Or is it a dream...?
I can't take it anymore.
When I get in the bath, the doll is in the tub with half its face sticking out of the water.
It won't leave my side for even a second.
Just when I thought I'd be better off dead, the doll gave me a wide grin.
And a voice echoed in my head.
'You die tomorrow...'
That was yesterday.
So, you see, today I'm going to die.
Which brings me to what I wanted to ask you..."{p}

He laughed again.
I couldn't look away anymore.
"...Actually, these sacrifices end next year.
Whoever becomes the sacrifice next year will be the last one.
Because that's what the doll says.
...Isn't that right?"{p}

With that, he abruptly pulled his face away from me and turned his eyes to my left shoulder.
I deliberately looked away from that direction.
My left shoulder, where nothing should have been, felt heavy.
Was the doll resting its face there?
Then Kanai brought his face close to mine again.{p}

"...It says so.
So I want you to make sure.
Whether that one is definitely at this school.
If they're here, there's no problem.
Then this school will finally be freed from its many curses.
I think the strange incidents that have happened at this school will stop, too.
The name is......"{p}

Just as Arai was about to tell us the rest...
The club room door suddenly opened.
"What are you all doing here at this hour?
This won't do. Dismissal time was ages ago."
The one who had opened the club room door and said that was the teacher on night duty.
"I'm sorry.
The newspaper club's interviews have taken a bit longer than we expected.
We'll be finished soon, so please, could we have a little more time?"
{f:I|I} bowed my head to the night-duty teacher.
"...Oh, all right.
But come and let me know in the night-duty room when you're done."
With that, the night-duty teacher left, grumbling a little.{p}

{f:I wondered|I wondered} if it was because we'd been caught staying so late.
Arai, somewhat flustered, began gathering up his things.

"Arai, you're in the middle of the story.
Please tell me the name of the person who'll be the sacrifice."
{f:I|I} asked, practically lunging at him.
As if {f:my|my} words weren't even reaching his ears, Arai hurried to leave the club room.
{f:I|I} grabbed his hand.
"Please.
What's that person's name★"
I pressed him.{p}
"That person is...

here, right now."
"What?"
"The last victim is among the people gathered here right now."
Arai smiled sadly.
"Kanai died of a heart attack.
Everyone, please be very careful.
This is as much as I can tell you..."{p}
Arai slipped out of {f:my|my} grip and ran off down the hallway as if fleeing.

{f:I|I} suddenly noticed.
Something was stuck to {f:my|my} right hand, the one I had grabbed his hand with.{p}

And then I thought.
Maybe this was the doll's...{p}

There's something about this school.
There must have been a reason the doll came to haunt this school, {f:too|too}.
The doll, the principal... what on earth is the connection between them{f:?|?}
In short, it must mean that doll is the root of the supernatural phenomena at this school{f:, but|, but}...

A school ruled by a doll... that's not a pleasant thought{f:.|.}{p}{f:But|But} what are we supposed to do, left hanging like this{f:?|?}
With these feelings of {f:ours|ours}...{p}

You don't want to hear it?
Then it can't be helped.
But in exchange, please grant me a request.{p}You'll grant my request, won't you?
Grant his request
Refuse his request

"My request is...
I want you to come with me, just the two of us, to the cherry tree behind the old school building.
Come on, let's go together."
Arai took {f:my|my} hand and pulled me along at a brisk pace.{p}

The cherry tree was in bloom out of season.
"Here we are."
With that, Arai planted himself right in front of {f:me|me}.
Then I felt something lukewarm and damp slide wetly across {f:my|my} eye.

"{f:Whoa|Eek}☆"
{f:I|I} cried out without thinking.
Again and again, the unknown thing touched {f:my|my} eyeball, as if licking it all over.
For some reason, {f:I|I} just let it lick my eyeball.
A thin film seemed to form over {f:my|my} eyes, and for a moment my vision blurred.{p}

But it cleared right away.
Soon, Arai came into view, peering at {f:me|me}.
"Arai, what is this?"
And then {f:I|I} gasped.{p}

Over Arai's shoulder was a doll with a white face.
The doll rested its chin on Arai's shoulder and stared at {f:me|me}.
Its eyes seemed unfocused{f:, yet|, yet} they held {f:me|me} firmly and wouldn't let go.
Then, the next moment, the face vanished.{p}

"Something touched your eye just now, didn't it?
That was the doll licking your eyeball all over.
Lucky you.
You've been chosen."
Arai broke into a broad smile.
"I mean, didn't you just see the doll's face on my shoulder?
Once it has sucked on your eyeballs and taken a liking to you, you become able to see it.
That's proof the sacrifice trade was a success."
{f:Hold on|Wait}, what do you mean, {f:a trade|a trade}★
Arai went on without a pause.
"Through some mistake, that doll ended up taking a liking to me.
But luckily, I heard that the sacrifice could be swapped.
I had only one chance...
Yes, the trade was a huge success."
{f:Wait|Wait} a minute!
{f:I'm|I'm}... {f:I'm|I'm} going to be the {f:sacrifice|sacrifice}★{p}

"The doll says you're the last sacrifice, the one who'll lift this school's curse.
In other words, you're the very last sacrifice.
You're a hero."
Arai said it as if it were someone else's problem.
{f:No way|No way} is that happening☆
{f:I'd|I'd} rather live a long life, even if this school's curse never gets lifted{f:!|!}
There's no way I'm throwing my life away over something like this{f:.|.}
"Do you want to trade too?
If you do, just do what I did, and with luck it'll work.
What? Well, because this only works once..."
{f:I|I} had no intention of listening to Arai anymore.
Because that doll was hanging from a branch of the cherry tree, watching {f:me|me}...{p}
...Look, over there.{p}

I see. This is the important part of the story, though.
Well, it can't be helped.
So you won't grant Kanai's request or mine...
Oh well, that's fine.
All I can do is pray that nothing bad happens to any of you.
...In the end, the seventh person never showed up.
Which means this meeting is over.
Well then, I'll be heading home first.
Excuse me.{p}
...With that, Arai got up from his seat as if fleeing.{p}

What should I do?
At this rate, he's going to leave.
Stop him
Let him go

"Please, wait!"
{f:I|I} grabbed Arai's shoulder to stop him.
"★"

When he turned around, his face was pure white.
What's more, expressionless eyes, large and mostly white, fixed on {f:me|me}.
It all happened in an instant, and {f:I|I} stood rooted to the spot.
Watching his back as he ran off...
What on earth was he...{p}This story ended with much of it still a mystery.
It was too late for regrets now{f:.|.}
It was {f:my|my} own fault for saying I didn't want to hear it.{p}

"Ah!"
Someone gave a small cry.
I looked at the table, and there lay a bundle of something like hair.
It looked as if someone had torn it out of their own head by force.
"Who put this {f:here|here}?"
{f:I|I} reached out for the bundle of hair.
Then, suddenly, the red cloth that had been draped over the table fell over {f:me|me}.{p}

"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
{f:I|I} struggled.
The cloth clung to {f:me|me} and wouldn't come off.
Suddenly, through the cloth, someone's hand traced {f:my|my} face.
"Everyone, stop fooling around!"
{f:I|I} said.
Then the cloth slid smoothly off {f:my|my} head.
{f:I|I} looked around, wondering who had done it.
"..........{f:You're kidding, right|This is a joke, right}?"
{f:I|I} muttered to myself.
There was no one in the chairs where everyone should have been sitting.{p}

{f:I|I} froze.
Because there, sitting all alone on a chair, was a small {f:child|child}.
Why would a child be in a place like this?
...No, this child wasn't human{f:.|.}
{f:Yes|Yes}, this was...
{f:I|I} understood at once.
This child was the doll Arai had told us about.{p}And at the same time, that {f:I|I} was the next sacrifice...{p}
